subject.title: Native Codex subagents hit `Native hook relay unavailable` on 2026.6.1 while parent session works

question: Should OpenClaw recover native Codex relay loss by falling back to generic policy/no-op paths, or should it preserve fail-closed behavior until relay refresh or re-registration succeeds?
rationale: This choice controls whether Codex native shell, patch, and MCP tools can proceed when the native hook relay is unavailable, and tests alone do not prove the security boundary in a real subagent/sandboxed setup.

options.title: Require Proven Recovery
options.body: Keep the issue open and require live subagent plus sandboxed MCP proof that native tools recover while approval policy, loop detection, and PermissionRequest behavior still enforce.

options.title: Accept Fallback Boundary
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept fallback-on-unavailable if they decide generic policy is the supported native tool boundary during relay loss.

options.title: Prefer Relay Refresh Only
options.body: Require a re-registration or relay-refresh design that keeps unknown relay-unavailable PreToolUse fail-closed until a current relay evaluates policy.

recommendation.title: Require Proven Recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require live subagent plus sandboxed MCP proof that native tools recover while approval policy, loop detection, and PermissionRequest behavior still enforce.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history and review comments place the guarded fallback contract and latest relay cleanup with steipete, making that person the best visible owner for the security-boundary choice.
